question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate that can inspect assistant text and hold risky tool calls before execution, or should this remain plugin/exec-policy-only for now?
rationale: The change adds config surface and alters the core tool authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core confirmation gate
options.body: Proceed with a backward-compatible core gate that composes with existing exec and plugin approval primitives and defines approve, deny, timeout, transcript, and channel behavior.

options.title: Keep plugin and exec primitives only
options.body: Decline a built-in gate for now and direct operators to existing exec approval settings or plugin policies for tool-specific confirmations.

options.title: Fold into generic HITL interrupt design
options.body: Move the work under the broader interrupt primitive in `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/83276`, accepting that this issue's same-response confirmation case must remain explicit acceptance criteria there.

recommendation.title: Design core confirmation gate
recommendation.body: Proceed with a backward-compatible core gate that composes with existing exec and plugin approval primitives and defines approve, deny, timeout, transcript, and channel behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline already routed this area to vincentkoc, and the remaining decision crosses hook/type and tool-policy surfaces where they have recent adjacent history.
